metric.why: Transformer and switchgear lead times stretched from months to years and now gate construction schedules as hard as permits do. Lead-time surveys are published by industry groups and research firms; watch the directory sources.
metric.definition: Order-to-delivery time for transformers, switchgear, generators, cooling plant, and high-end accelerators.

reading.body:
Critical equipment lead times now gate data center construction schedules as hard as permits do. Transformers, switchgear, generators, and cooling plant have moved from months to years on order-to-delivery.

That shift matters because a data center is a building full of power equipment before it is a building full of servers. Compute capacity cannot come online faster than the long-lead electrical and cooling components arrive, no matter how quickly accelerators are available. The metric tracks both the heavy infrastructure and the high-end accelerators, which puts the two halves of a build on the same clock.

The data here is a definition and a direction, not a series. It states that lead times stretched from months to years and that surveys exist, but it gives no figures, no dates, and no named sources. It does not say which component is scarcest, whether the trend is still worsening, or how lead times vary by region or vendor. Readers should treat it as a pointer to the underlying surveys rather than as evidence in itself.
